page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.1-16 is a flexible x86_64 virtual machine instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory. The underlying hardware runs on an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor with a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The 2 vCPUs map directly to 1 physical core utilizing multithreading with 2 threads per core, providing dedicated rather than burstable or shared CPU allocation. The instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address for external network connectivity.

The configuration provides an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB of RAM allocated per virtual core, making it memory-dense relative to its compute capacity. There is no integrated local NVMe storage and no discrete GPU hardware attached, requiring persistence and high-throughput IOPS to be delivered via remote block volume storage. This architecture maintains cost efficiency by avoiding charges for unused local disks or acceleration hardware while scaling RAM independently of CPU count.

Given its elevated memory footprint paired with single-core execution capacity, VM.Standard.E5.Flex.1-16 fits memory-bound applications that require minimal parallel processing. Suitable operational deployments include lightweight database instances, Redis or in-memory caches, small-scale ETL microservices, development environments, and low-traffic backend web services that consume significant memory footprints.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.1-16 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The instance delivers 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical execution core via 2 threads per core, accompanied by 16.0 GB of system memory. This produces an 8.0 GB per-core allocation, favoring memory-intensive operations over raw compute density. The server includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address and features no attached local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, necessitating external block storage for persistent data. By decoupling high memory capacity from massive vCPU counts, the instance provides qualitative resource efficiency for lightweight operational architectures. VM.Standard.E5.Flex.1-16 is tailored for workloads requiring elevated memory footprints without heavy parallel processing, including small in-memory caches, entry-level relational databases, background data ingestion tasks, and memory-dependent web application services.
